name: Electric-Assist Bicycle
description: A single category, not the three-class system: a low-speed electrically assisted bicycle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts that assists only while the rider pedals, to a top motor-powered speed under 20 mph. It's regulated as a bicycle.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts (one horsepower)
Top motor-powered speed under 20 mph, measured with a 170-pound rider on a paved level surface
No throttle: the motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
No class system: South Carolina has not adopted the three-class model law
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently label it with its wattage and top assisted speed; owners may not remove or tamper with the label
Anyone who modifies it to change its speed must replace the label to match

Riders under 21 on a two-wheeled one may need a helmet and goggles: the law requiring them covers any two-wheeled motorized vehicle and doesn't exempt e-bikes, but it sits among the motorcycle rules and the code doesn't say whether it reaches them
Carries only as many riders as it's designed and equipped for
Not a moped, and the bicyclist rules apply to it, but the code doesn't say whether it needs a driver's license, registration or insurance
Rides by the same rules as a bicycle, including using an adjacent bicycle lane where one is provided

Treats a stop sign as a yield sign; at a red light it may go through after a full stop once no traffic is an immediate hazard, turn right after slowing without stopping, or turn left onto a one-way road after stopping
restrictions.citation: South Carolina Code §§56-5-970(C)(6), 56-5-3530, enacted by 2026 Act No. 173 (S.812)

restrictions.rule: One whose motor exceeds 750 W, up to 1,500 W, is a moped, which needs a driver's or moped license and registration
